text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Several of the guides I found agree on this, and the sources are mostly retailer-affiliated review sites plus some cited lab research.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-4,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-800 for NMC. At one full cycle a day, that's about 8-11 years versus under 2 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. In one test, the LFP cell peaked at 259 °C versus 731 °C for NMC. LFP isn't fireproof, but it's the better choice for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One site's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is much cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC is mostly in older stock and small, light units.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Cell-level energy density:** NMC cells store more energy per pound. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% difference in the median, and some LFP models are lighter per Wh than NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare the actual specs of the models you're considering.

**Things to watch**
- **Cold weather:** Both chemistries generally won't charge below 32°F, and the limits depend more on the brand than the chemistry. Check the manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One guide claims LFP handles cold much better, but others contradict that.
- **Cycle ratings:** Compare the end point too. "3,000 cycles to 80%" promises more than "4,000 to 70%".
- **Chemistry not stated:** Some listings don't name it, so verify before buying.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Outage kit used a few times a year:** Either works, since age matters more than cycles. Take LFP if the price is similar.
- **Weight-critical and rarely used:** Compare specific models. An NMC unit can make sense, but only at a clearly lower price.

I can also shortlist specific LiFePO4 models for your use case and budget. Let me know the capacity you need and what you'll run.
